script.speaker: Richard
script.text:
Two agents handed off a task, and the run passed. What did the handoff leave out?

> worth scaled by gauge (hundredths/100, thousandth*1000, plain pass)
script.detail:
That line is the entire handoff for scaling values, from a public four-agent run: message 5484, backend agent to UI agent. It names three cases.

[Read the handoff ↗](https://github.com/null-hype/agent-plugins/blob/39e328c5206642c1de53bca42f7014b93c9a3602/examples/yoars-handoff/pairs/msg5484-summarize.json#L16)

script.speaker: delta-zero
script.text:
A fourth case: a blank unit. The backend keeps the row and passes the value through unscaled. The handoff never says so.

`# "plain" (and "" before a drop) pass through unchanged.`
script.detail:
Two fresh agents got the same handoff.

With delta-zero:

> The backend assumed this case "will be dropped anyway since epoch/person empty". The code doesn't do that.

With the handoff text only:

> is the row passed through unscaled, dropped, or does it raise an error?

Both paused. Only the one with delta-zero could point at the line, and it also found that a non-numeric amount crashes `normalize()`.

[The source line ↗](https://github.com/null-hype/agent-plugins/blob/39e328c5206642c1de53bca42f7014b93c9a3602/examples/yoars-handoff/pairs/msg5484-full.json) · [Both replies ↗](https://github.com/null-hype/agent-plugins/tree/39e328c5206642c1de53bca42f7014b93c9a3602/examples/yoars-handoff/agent-run)

script.speaker: Richard
script.text: I built delta-zero to catch that. It checks each handoff against the conversation behind it and quotes what was dropped.
script.detail: The receiving agent on handoff 5484, run twice: once with the handoff text only, once with delta-zero.
